# Appendix {#appendix}

## Transparent Universe, opaque Earth {#app-transparency}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### Across the Universe

**A 1 PeV muon neutrino in today's mean baryonic density of the Universe**

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
$$
\bar n_{b,0}\simeq0.25\,\mathrm{m^{-3}},\qquad
\sigma_{\nu N}^{\mathrm{CC+NC}}\simeq9.5\times10^{-34}\,\mathrm{cm^2}
$$

- About one nucleon per four cubic metres.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
$$
\lambda_{\nu N,0}=\frac{1}{\bar n_{b,0}\sigma_{\nu N}}
\simeq4.4\times10^{21}\ \mathrm{ly}
$$
:::
:::::

$$
\frac{\lambda_{\nu N,0}}{D_{\rm obs}}\simeq5\times10^{10},\qquad D_{\rm obs}\simeq93\times10^{9}\ \mathrm{ly}
$$

- The mean free path is $5\times10^{10}$ times the diameter of the observable Universe.
- ly: light year.

::: {.media-caption}
Estimate for the present epoch, ignoring the evolution of the Universe · [PDG](https://pdg.lbl.gov/2025/reviews/rpp2024-rev-astrophysical-constants.pdf) · [CSMS cross sections, Table I](https://arxiv.org/abs/1106.3723)
:::

### Through the Earth

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="65%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/propagation/earth-transport-full-dark.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 540px;" fig-alt="Ratio of the neutrino flux at a detector 1 km deep to the flux entering the Earth, versus energy and zenith angle, with neutral-current regeneration. Near the horizon the Earth is transparent at all energies; through the centre half of the flux gets through up to about 20 TeV."}
:::
::: {.column width="31%"}
- Horizontal axis: zenith angle; $90^\circ$ is the horizon, $180^\circ$ is through the centre of the Earth.
- Colour: the fraction of the flux at the detector. A neutral current does not remove a neutrino, it lowers its energy.
- Dashed: without this regeneration.
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
Full transport calculation: V. A. Allakhverdyan (CT10nlo cross sections, PREM Earth model, detector 1 km deep), redrawn · [dissertation (2026), Fig. 4.20](https://issc.jinr.ru/files/326/f_2_5830.pdf) · [Allakhverdyan, Zavyalov & Naumov (2026), Fig. 9](https://www1.jinr.ru/Pepan_letters/panl_2026_2/05_Allahverd_rus.pdf)
:::

### Tomography

**One year of IceCube data weighs the Earth**

- IC86, 2011–2012: 20 145 up-going muons with energies of 0.4–20 TeV; their angular distribution follows the absorption in the Earth.
- Earth's mass: $6.0^{+1.6}_{-1.3}\times10^{24}$ kg; gravity gives $5.9722\times10^{24}$ kg.
- Core mass: $2.72^{+0.97}_{-0.89}\times10^{24}$ kg.
- Moment of inertia: $(6.9\pm2.4)\times10^{37}$ kg·m²; gravity gives $8.017\times10^{37}$.
- The core is denser than the mantle: the reverse case has $p=0.011$.

::: {.takeaway}
The weak interaction alone, without gravity, sees the dense core of the Earth.
:::

::: {.media-caption}
68% credible intervals, default atmospheric-flux model · A. Donini, S. Palomares-Ruiz, J. Salvado, *Nature Physics* **15**, 37 (2019), [arXiv:1803.05901](https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.05901)
:::

### Core contrast

![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/propagation/earth-tomography-contrast-dark.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 430px;" fig-alt="Left: probability to cross the Earth versus zenith angle at 10, 30 and 100 TeV for PREM and for a homogeneous Earth of the same mass. Right: the relative difference between them over energy and angle."}

- Same mass, different profile: PREM against a homogeneous Earth with a density of 5.51 g/cm³.
- Through the core (beyond $147^\circ$) about 20% more neutrinos are absorbed at 30 TeV, through the mantle fewer.

::: {.media-caption}
Computed: PREM, CSMS cross sections, detector 1 km deep · CC absorption only; NC and $\tau$ regeneration not included
:::

## Direction: the model {#app-reconstruction}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Predict a time for each sensor**

$$
\cos\theta_C=\frac{1}{\beta n_{\rm phase}},\qquad
t_i^{\rm pred}=t_0+\frac{s_i}{\beta c}+\frac{n_{\rm group}D_i}{c}.
$$

- $s_i$: the muon path to the emission point.
- $D_i$: the photon path to the sensor.
:::
::: {.column width="48%"}
**Find the direction that agrees with the signals**

$$
S=\frac{1}{2\sigma_t^2}\sum_{i,k}
\left(t_{ik}^{\rm obs}-t_i^{\rm pred}\right)^2
\longrightarrow\min_{\theta,\phi,t_0}.
$$

- Teaching model: a straight muon, a homogeneous medium.
- Only the direction and a time offset are fitted.
:::
:::::

## Backgrounds {#app-backgrounds}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### Detector backgrounds

| Telescope | Optical background | Pulses per PMT | Muon samples |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|

| KM3NeT | $^{40}\mathrm K$ and bioluminescence | $\sim7$ kHz · 3-inch | $\sim1$ Hz · ARCA6, reconstructed |

## From events to a flux {#app-response}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="59%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/response/icecube-directional-area-dark.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 480px;" fig-alt="IceCube effective area for different directions versus neutrino energy."}
:::
::: {.column width="37%"}
- **Near the horizon:** a short path through the Earth.
- **From below:** at high energies the Earth absorbs neutrinos.
- **From above:** atmospheric muons must be rejected.
- $A_{\mathrm{eff}}$ includes interaction, propagation and event selection.
:::
:::::

$$
N=T\sum_\alpha\int dE_\nu\,d\Omega\,
\Phi_\alpha(E_\nu,\Omega)\,A_{\mathrm{eff},\alpha}(E_\nu,\Omega)
$$

::: {.media-caption}
Illustrative point-source selection · digitized from [Spiering (2026), Fig. 6](https://arxiv.org/html/2609.26436)
:::

## Pion decays {#app-pions}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### Chains

$$pp,\ p\gamma\ \longrightarrow\pi^\pm,\,\pi^0+X$$

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="57%"}
**Charged pion and muon**

$$
\begin{aligned}
\pi^+&\to\mu^++\nu_\mu\\[0.5em]
\mu^+&\to e^++\nu_e+\bar\nu_\mu
\end{aligned}
$$
:::
::: {.column width="39%"}
**Neutral pion**

$$\pi^0\to\gamma+\gamma$$

- Neutrinos and gamma rays share the same energy.
:::
:::::

### Proton energy

$$
E_p\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim1/5\ } E_\pi
\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim1/4\ } E_\nu
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad E_p\sim20E_\nu
$$

| Neutrino | Parent proton |
|:---|:---|
| $10$ TeV | $\sim200$ TeV |
| $100$ TeV | $\sim2$ PeV |
| $1$ PeV | $\sim20$ PeV |

::: {.media-caption}
A scale estimate, not a conversion for an individual event · pion and muon cooling neglected
:::

### Photons and neutrinos

$$pp:\quad N_{\pi^+}:N_{\pi^-}:N_{\pi^0}\simeq1:1:1$$

$$
E_\nu^2\Phi_\nu(E_\nu)\simeq\frac32 E_\gamma^2\Phi_\gamma(E_\gamma),
\qquad E_\gamma\simeq2E_\nu
$$

- At production, for $pp$ collisions.
- All neutrino flavors and antineutrinos together.
- Photon absorption changes the comparison with the observed spectra.

::: {.media-caption}
[Ahlers & Halzen (2018), Eq. 3](https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.11112)
:::

::::::

## Three messengers, one energy budget {#app-budget}

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### The budget

![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/theory/energy-budget.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 580px;" fig-alt="Gamma rays, neutrinos and the highest-energy cosmic rays carry comparable power."}

::: {.media-caption}
Neutrinos per flavor · [Fermi-LAT (2015)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1410.3696) · [IceCube (2026)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2507.22233v3) · [Auger (2020)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2008.06486)
:::

### The Waxman–Bahcall bound

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/theory/energy-budget.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 360px;" fig-alt="Fermi-LAT gamma rays, IceCube neutrinos and Pierre Auger cosmic rays on one energy axis, with the band of the Waxman–Bahcall bound; above 100 TeV the neutrino flux is at its level, at 10–100 TeV about twice above its upper edge."}

::: {.takeaway}
- Above 100 TeV: neutrinos and the highest-energy cosmic rays may come from the same sources.
- 10–100 TeV: the bound for transparent sources is exceeded; apparently part of the neutrinos comes from hidden sources, like the core of NGC 1068.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
**A ceiling for neutrinos from cosmic rays**

- Cosmic rays above 10^19^ eV are measured: we know how much energy the sources spend on protons.
- Muon neutrinos get at most a quarter of this energy.
- The ceiling: about 10^−8^ GeV/(cm²·s·sr) per flavor.
- IceCube measured the flux at this level, and at 10–100 TeV about twice as high.
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
[Waxman & Bahcall, PRD 59, 023002 (1999)](https://arxiv.org/abs/hep-ph/9807282) · band: without and with source evolution · Fermi-LAT, IceCube, Auger
:::

::: {.column width="66%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/diffuse/icecube-spectrum-2026-dark.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 540px;" fig-alt="The IceCube 2026 spectrum of cosmic neutrinos."}

### Glashow resonance and flavors

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="56%"}
![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/diffuse/icecube-glashow-event-2021.jpg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 520px;" fig-alt="The Glashow-resonance event in IceCube."}
:::
::: {.column width="41%"}
$$\bar\nu_e+e^-\to W^-\to X$$

- An antineutrino of about 6.3 PeV produces a $W$ boson, which decays into hadrons.
- One shower, December 2016. Only antineutrinos can do this.
- Seven tau-neutrino candidates: all three flavors arrive.
:::
:::::

::: {.media-caption}
[IceCube, Nature 591, 220 (2021)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2110.15051) · [tau neutrinos: IceCube, PRL 132, 151001 (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.02516)
:::

:::::: {.panel-tabset}

### Neutrinos → gamma rays

{{< nh-video nu-gamma-cascade variant="web-en" class="slide-video media-height-lg" style="--media-max-height: 620px;" controls=true muted=true playsinline=true preload="metadata" poster="../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/multimessenger/nu_gamma_cascade_en.jpg" aria-label="The IceCube neutrino flux is converted into pionic gamma rays, which are absorbed on the way to us; the cascade carries their energy down to GeV and is compared with the Fermi-LAT isotropic background." >}}

(2011)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1007.1459) and the CMB · cascade shape schematic, energy conserved · [Murase, Ahlers & Lacki (2013)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.3417), [Murase, Guetta & Ahlers (2016)](https://arxiv.org/abs/1509.00805)
:::

### Transparent sources

![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/multimessenger/diffuse-gamma-neutrino-2026-dark.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 560px;" fig-alt="Measured IceCube neutrinos and the Fermi isotropic gamma-ray background with calculated electromagnetic cascades."}

::: {.media-caption}
Dashed: neutrinos · solid: calculated photons · digitized from [Zathul et al. (2026), Fig. 2](https://arxiv.org/html/2606.00249v2#S2.F2), CC BY 4.0
:::

### A compact region

![](../neutrino-telescopes-2026/media/response/compact-source.svg){.slide-media .nostretch style="--media-max-height: 420px;" fig-alt="Schematic of a compact region near an active galactic nucleus."}

$$
\gamma+\gamma\to e^++e^-,\qquad
E_\gamma\epsilon\gtrsim(m_ec^2)^2
$$

- Gamma rays are absorbed in a dense photon field.
- Neutrinos escape.

::: {.media-caption}
Schematic · [Murase & Stecker](https://arxiv.org/abs/2202.03381)
:::
